next_state_election.name: Statewide General Election
next_state_election.source_name: Rhode Island Board of Elections — Upcoming Elections

glance_notes.source_name: Rhode Island Board of Elections — Upcoming Elections
glance_notes.text: 2026 General Election Registration Deadline: Rhode Island's voter registration deadline for the November 3, 2026 General Election is October 4. Eligible residents should register or update their voter record by that date to vote in all contests on the General Election ballot.

glance_notes.source_name: Rhode Island Board of Elections — In-Person Early Voting
glance_notes.text: Early Voting Begins October 14: Rhode Island provides in-person early voting during the 20 days before Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, early voting begins October 14 and ends at 4:00 p.m. November 2.

glance_notes.source_name: Rhode Island Board of Elections — Voter ID
glance_notes.text: Photo ID Required In Person: Rhode Island requires voters to present an acceptable photo ID when voting in person. A voter without acceptable photo identification may cast a provisional ballot. Identification is not required when voting by mail.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Rhode Island residents may register online or submit a paper voter registration form. Online registration requires a Rhode Island DMV-issued driver's license or state identification number. A person without one may complete a registration form for paper submission. To register, a person must be a U.S. citizen and Rhode Island resident, be at least 16 years old, not be incarcerated in a correctional facility upon a felony conviction and not have been judged mentally incompetent to vote by a court. A person may preregister beginning at age 16 but must be at least 18 years old to vote.
register.glance_value: Online or paper registration; preregistration at 16
register.source_name: Rhode Island Department of State — Register to Vote
register.internal_note: Rhode Island's current registration portal directly states the citizenship, residency, age, felony-incarceration and mental-competency requirements. Rhode Island restores voting eligibility after release from incarceration following a felony conviction; probation and parole do not by themselves prevent registration. Do not state that a person must complete probation or parole before registering.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Use Rhode Island's Voter Information Center to view your voter record and confirm that your registration information is current. The system allows voters to update voter information, track a mail ballot, map their polling place, preview a sample ballot and print a voter information card.
check_registration.glance_value: Check your record in the Voter Information Center
check_registration.source_name: Rhode Island Department of State — My Voter Record
check_registration.internal_note: The current Voter Information Center directly lists voter-record updates, mail-ballot tracking, polling-place mapping, sample-ballot preview and voter information card functions.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: Rhode Island generally requires voter registration at least 30 days before an election. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the registration deadline is Sunday, October 4. A person who misses the deadline may have limited presidential-election voting rights under Rhode Island law, but should not expect to vote in all federal, state and local contests without timely registration.
deadlines.source_name: Rhode Island Board of Elections — Upcoming Elections
deadlines.internal_note: The Board of Elections' current 2026 schedule directly establishes October 4 as the General Election voter registration deadline. Rhode Island has a special presidential-only exception for certain otherwise eligible voters who miss the ordinary registration deadline. Do not characterize that exception as general same-day registration because it does not provide access to the full ballot.

polling_place.label: Find a Polling Place
polling_place.content: Use Rhode Island's Voter Information Center to find the Election Day polling place assigned to your residential address and confirm its hours. The lookup also provides a sample ballot for the address. Polling locations can change, so voters should verify their assigned location shortly before Election Day.
polling_place.source_name: Rhode Island Department of State — Polling Place & Sample Ballot Lookup
polling_place.internal_note: The official address-based lookup provides polling location, polling hours and sample-ballot information. Reverify November 2026 locations near Election Day because local boards of canvassers administer polling places.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Rhode Island's Statewide General Election is Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Most polling places open at 7:00 a.m. and all close at 8:00 p.m. New Shoreham is the General Election exception and opens at 9:00 a.m. Voters should check the official polling-place lookup for their exact location and opening time. In-person voters must present acceptable photo identification. A voter without acceptable photo ID may cast a provisional ballot.
election_day.glance_value: Most polls 7:00 a.m. – 8:00 p.m.; New Shoreham opens at 9:00 a.m.
election_day.source_name: Rhode Island Board of Elections — General Election Polling Place Hours
election_day.internal_note: Important exception: do not say every Rhode Island polling place opens at 7:00 a.m. The Board of Elections' municipality-by-municipality General Election schedule shows every listed municipality opening at 7:00 a.m. except New Shoreham, which opens at 9:00 a.m. All listed municipalities close at 8:00 p.m. The Department of State accordingly describes polling places as typically opening at 7:00 a.m. and instructs voters to confirm their specific opening time.

polling_hours.label: Polling Hours
polling_hours.content: Rhode Island General Election polling places close at 8:00 p.m. Most municipalities open polling places at 7:00 a.m. New Shoreham opens at 9:00 a.m. for a General Election. Voters should use the official polling-place lookup to confirm the exact hours for their assigned location.
polling_hours.glance_value: Most: 7:00 a.m. – 8:00 p.m.; New Shoreham: 9:00 a.m. – 8:00 p.m.
polling_hours.source_name: Rhode Island Board of Elections — General Election Polling Place Hours
polling_hours.internal_note: The Board of Elections explicitly lists the General Election hours municipality by municipality. The New Shoreham exception is real and should remain in the record rather than simplifying Rhode Island to a uniform 7:00 a.m.-8:00 p.m. schedule.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: Rhode Island provides in-person early voting during the 20 days leading up to Election Day. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, early voting begins October 14 and ends at 4:00 p.m. November 2. Early voting typically takes place at the voter's city or town hall or another location designated by the local Board of Canvassers. Voters must present acceptable photo identification when voting early. Early ballots are cast into a voting tabulator but are not tabulated until after polls close on Election Night. Locations and daily hours vary by municipality and should be confirmed before voting.
early_voting.source_name: Rhode Island Board of Elections — In-Person Early Voting
early_voting.internal_note: The Board of Elections confirms a 20-day early-voting period and the 2026 election calendar establishes October 14 through November 2 at 4:00 p.m. for the General Election. Local locations and hours vary. Rhode Island law and election materials sometimes use emergency voting terminology in connection with this period, but current Board guidance explicitly calls the in-person option early voting.

absentee_mail.label: Mail Ballot Voting
absentee_mail.content: Rhode Island allows any otherwise qualified registered voter to choose to vote by mail. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, a regular mail-ballot application must be received by the voter's local Board of Canvassers by October 13. Voters who need a mail ballot after that deadline may qualify to apply for an emergency mail ballot through their local Board of Canvassers until 4:00 p.m. November 2. Completed regular mail ballots must be received by the Rhode Island Board of Elections or placed in an authorized elections drop box no later than 8:00 p.m. on Election Day. A postmark by Election Day is not enough if the ballot arrives after the deadline.
absentee_mail.glance_value: Request by October 13; ballot due by 8:00 p.m. November 3
absentee_mail.source_name: Rhode Island Board of Elections — Mail Ballot
absentee_mail.internal_note: Rhode Island's current mail-ballot application expressly includes the category 'I choose to vote by mail,' so no excuse is required. The official 2026 election calendar establishes October 13 as the regular application deadline, November 2 at 4:00 p.m. as the emergency application deadline and November 3 at 8:00 p.m. as the regular ballot receipt deadline. The ballot must be received; there is no ordinary postmark grace period.

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Rhode Island requires valid photo identification when voting in person, including during early voting. Accepted identification includes a Rhode Island driver's license or permit, Rhode Island Voter ID card, U.S. passport, identification issued by a U.S. educational institution, U.S. military identification, identification issued by the U.S. government or State of Rhode Island, a government-issued medical card and identification issued by a federally recognized tribal government. Identification generally cannot have expired more than six months before the election. Rhode Island Driving Privilege Cards and Permits are not accepted as voter identification. A voter without acceptable photo ID may cast a provisional ballot. Identification is not required to vote by mail.
voter_id.glance_value: Photo ID required in person; provisional ballot available
voter_id.source_name: Rhode Island Board of Elections — Voter ID
voter_id.internal_note: The Board of Elections updated its voter-ID guidance in July 2026. It directly confirms the accepted categories, provisional-ballot procedure and that identification is not required for mail voting. The Department of State offers a free Rhode Island Voter ID card to eligible voters who lack another accepted form. Driving Privilege Cards and Permits are specifically excluded.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Rhode Island provides accessible voting options and assistance for voters with disabilities. In-person voters may use the ExpressVote ballot-marking system to mark a ballot privately and independently. Voters who need assistance may receive help under Rhode Island's voting-assistance procedures. Accessible mail-ballot options are also available for qualifying voters, and an Accessible Mail Ballot Request Form is provided by the Department of State for use with a mail-ballot application. Voters with accessibility questions may contact their local Board of Canvassers or the Rhode Island Department of State Elections Division.
accessible_voting.glance_value: ExpressVote and accessible mail-ballot options available
accessible_voting.source_name: Rhode Island Department of State — Vote on Election Day
accessible_voting.internal_note: The Department of State's current Election Day guidance specifically identifies ExpressVote as the accessible ballot-marking option. Its 2026 forms page provides an Accessible Mail Ballot Request Form that must be filed with a mail-ballot application. Do not describe accessible electronic ballot marking as unrestricted online ballot return.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Rhode Island provides special voting procedures for eligible members of the Uniformed Services, qualifying family members and U.S. citizens living outside the United States. Covered voters may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request a ballot and may use federal military and overseas voting procedures when applicable. Rhode Island's 2026 election materials provide special ballot-delivery and return procedures for these voters. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, qualifying military and overseas ballots may be received by the Rhode Island Board of Elections through 4:00 p.m. November 10 when returned in accordance with the applicable military and overseas voting rules.
military_overseas.glance_value: Qualifying UOCAVA ballots may be received through November 10 at 4:00 p.m.
military_overseas.source_name: Rhode Island Department of State — Elections Publications and Forms
military_overseas.internal_note: The Department of State's 2026 forms page provides the Federal Post Card Application for military and overseas voters. The official 2026 Election Calendar states that November 10 at 4:00 p.m. is the final receipt deadline for qualifying military and overseas General Election mail ballots under RIGL 17-20-16. Do not apply this seven-day extension to ordinary domestic mail ballots, which are due by 8:00 p.m. Election Day.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: College students may register in Rhode Island if they meet the state's voter eligibility and residency requirements. A student who establishes a Rhode Island residence for voting purposes may register using that residence, while a student who maintains a qualifying voting residence elsewhere may vote under the rules applicable to that residence. Students should register and vote from only one residence in an election. A student voting in person in Rhode Island may use an identification card issued by a U.S. educational institution as an acceptable form of voter photo identification.
student_voting.glance_value: Qualifying student ID accepted for in-person voting
student_voting.source_name: Rhode Island Board of Elections — Voter ID
student_voting.internal_note: The current Board of Elections voter-ID page explicitly includes an ID issued by a U.S. educational institution among accepted photo identification. General Rhode Island registration and residency rules apply to students. Avoid claiming that merely attending a Rhode Island college automatically establishes Rhode Island voting residency.

sample_ballot.label: Official Sample Ballot
sample_ballot.content: Rhode Island voters can use the Voter Information Center to preview the sample ballot associated with their residential address. The polling-place lookup also provides the voter's Election Day location and hours. Because ballot contents depend on the voter's district and municipality, voters should use their own address or voter record to retrieve the applicable November 3, 2026 ballot after it is finalized.
sample_ballot.glance_value: Preview your ballot in the Voter Information Center
sample_ballot.source_name: Rhode Island Department of State — Polling Place & Sample Ballot Lookup
sample_ballot.internal_note: The official Voter Information Center directly provides address-based sample-ballot lookup. The Board of Elections' Upcoming Elections page also publishes sample ballots when available. Reverify after the November General Election ballots are finalized.

contact.label: Contact Rhode Island Election Officials
contact.content: Rhode Island election responsibilities are divided between the Department of State Elections Division, the Rhode Island Board of Elections and local Boards of Canvassers. The Rhode Island Board of Elections is located at 2000 Plainfield Pike, Cranston, RI 02921. Phone: 401-222-2345. Fax: 401-222-3135. For voter registration, voter records, polling-place information and other voter services, voters may also contact the Rhode Island Department of State Elections Division or their local Board of Canvassers.
contact.internal_note: Rhode Island divides election administration among multiple authorities, so describing only the Secretary of State as the sole state election authority would be misleading. The Board of Elections currently lists 2000 Plainfield Pike, Cranston, RI 02921; phone 401-222-2345; fax 401-222-3135. Department of State voter-ID assistance uses 401-222-2340. No email address was inserted unless independently verified as current.

official_resources.label: Official State & Local Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Rhode Island Department of State Voter Information Center and Rhode Island Board of Elections for official election information. The Voter Information Center provides registration, voter-record lookup, polling places, sample ballots, mail-ballot requests and tracking, early-voting information and election resources. The Board of Elections provides election dates, mail-ballot information, voter-ID guidance, early-voting information and election-administration resources. Local Boards of Canvassers administer voter registration and many local voting functions.
official_resources.glance_value: Voter Information Center, Board of Elections & local Boards of Canvassers
